supporting_observations.claim: The alerted periodic HTTPS activity is attributable to PID 3132, running routewiseupd.exe from kim.nguyen's user-profile AppData directory, with explorer.exe as its parent.

The updater process connected through the proxy to update.routewise.co:443. The inventory identifies the approved RouteWise update host as update.routewise.com and the approved updater location as C:\Program Files\RouteWise\routewiseupd.exe; both the observed hostname and executable location differ.
The same process made repeated proxy connections to update.routewise.co at roughly five-minute intervals, including 13:37, 13:43, 13:47, 13:53, 13:57, 14:02, and 14:07 UTC.

The regular cadence resembles the approved RouteWise update-check behavior, but the observed hostname and user-writable executable path do not match the approved service details. This combination supports treating the alerted activity as malicious rather than as the approved updater.

known_telemetry_limitations: Winsec collection on DC-COP-01 was unavailable from 13:30 to 14:00 UTC according to the supplied sensor status. The alerted connections are nevertheless represented in proxy, Zeek, and workstation Sysmon records.

The proxy records show HTTPS CONNECT tunnels and byte counts, not the tunneled request or response contents; the available records therefore do not establish what data or payload, if any, was exchanged.
claims_not_established: The binary's hash, signature, provenance, and whether it is a modified or counterfeit RouteWise updater are not established by the available records.
The ownership or intent of update.routewise.co, and whether it delivered malicious content, are not established.
The contents of the HTTPS exchanges and whether any information was exfiltrated are not established.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire and analyze the routewiseupd.exe file, including its hash, digital signature, origin, and any version or update artifacts.
Review DNS resolution, TLS certificate and reputation data, and proxy or endpoint network telemetry for update.routewise.co.
Retrieve endpoint and proxy content or inspection evidence, if available, for the observed sessions; assess for downloaded files, persistence, or follow-on execution.
Investigate the workstation for other activity associated with PID 3132 and the same destination, including evidence outside the supplied time window.
unrelated_findings: At 14:08 UTC, kim.nguyen obtained a Kerberos service ticket for WS-PBECKER-01 and logged on to that host with a network logon from 10.52.10.24. Given the inventory's remote-administration practice, review this separately; it does not determine the alerted RouteWise-like connections. (T135-00274, T135-00275)

DropboxUpdate.exe ran as SYSTEM on WS-KNGUYEN-01. Dropbox is not among the approved services, but these records alone do not show Dropbox file-sharing activity or connect it to the alert. (T135-00176, T135-00177)
